note: Track open-chords (guitar-basic-chords), step 3: Em, Am, E, A and D together: the five shapes from memory, minor next to major, then ten bars that meet every pair of the five once, one strum a bar.

exercise.title: Five open chords, any two in a row
exercise.why: Every change between two chords is its own move, so the last block plays the five chords in an order where each one meets every other once, and the changes that are still slow show up.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it. Fret each of the five chords in turn, and look at its chord box only after your fingers are down.
Keep going until every shape lands without a look.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down once on beat 1, then use the rest of the bar to move to the next chord.
When Em changes to E and Am to A, listen for the one note that goes up.

Press Play below to start the metronome. The ten bars hold the five chords in an order where every chord meets each of the others once: strum down once on beat 1, then move.
If a change comes late, keep counting and catch the next beat 1.
